newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MILAN ACKNOWLEDGES THAT BAGGIO MIGHT LEAVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN ACKNOWLEDGES THAT BAGGIO MIGHT LEAVE.

text.p: AC Milan said on Friday that Roberto Baggio might leave the Italian serie A club before the start of next season but Montenegrin Dejan Savicevic was set to stay.
"Baggio's future depends on him," Milan managing director Adriano Galliani told reporters.
"He still has a year left on his contract but he knows how the coach views the situation. His agents are discussing various possible deals but there is still nothing definitive."

Baggio, 30, said on Wednesday that coach Fabio Capello, making big changes since returning to Milan after a season with Spanish champions Real Madrid, had told him by phone that he was not part of future plans.
The 1994 World Cup star has been linked to Napoli, Sampdoria and Vicenza, the club where he started his professional career, as well as Spain's Barcelona.
Italian newspapers reported earlier this week that Capello had also told Savicevic, whose contract expires in 1998, that he would not be needed in the new Milan.
But Galliani said the mercurial playmaker, who is reported to have rejected offers from Olympiakos of Greece and France's Marseille, would be staying.
"There is no 'Savicevic affair'. He will remain a Milan player," Galliani said.

He said Milan had given up hopes of signing Sampdoria's French international Christian Karembeu, who is sought by both Real Madrid and Barcelona, and had little expectation of bringing Christian Panucci back to Milan.
Milan sold the Italy defender early last season to Real and newspapers said Capello had wanted to bring him back to Milan.
Capello was tempted back to Italy after Milan suffered one of their worst runs ever, ending last season in the bottom half of the table.
